Terms of Service

Last updated November 23, 2026

These are the Terms of Service for Petto. By adding Petto to a server, or using any of its commands, you agree to everything below.

1. Using Petto

  1. Petto is provided as-is, free to add to a Discord server. As-is means you use the bot in the state it is in at each moment, with the features it has and any errors it may have.
  2. Features can change, break, or be removed at any point while the bot is in active development. A command or an option that works today can work differently, or stop existing, after an update.
  3. Adding Petto to a server, or using any of its commands, means you accept these terms. This applies both to the people who add the bot and to the members who only use its commands.

2. Eligibility

  1. You need to meet Discord's own minimum age requirement (13, or higher where local law requires it) to use Discord, and by extension Petto.
  2. Petto does not set a different age of its own. If Discord does not allow you to have an account where you live, you may not use Petto either.
  3. Server owners are responsible for making sure their members meet that requirement too. It is part of running a Discord server, in the same way as following Discord's own rules.

3. Your server, your responsibility

  1. Server owners and admins are responsible for how they configure Petto on their server.
  2. That covers automated messages, custom commands, reaction roles, moderation actions, and anything else set up through it, whether it was set up with commands such as `!customcommand` and `!reactionrole` or in the dashboard.
  3. Petto executes what it is configured to do; it does not review configuration for intent. If an automatic message or a custom command is set up to post something harmful, Petto posts it, and the responsibility is with whoever set it up.
  4. Before turning on an automation, check what it will do and who can trigger it. Commands you do not want on your server can be turned off with `!disablecommand`.

4. Statistics and analysis

  1. Petto can count the activity of a server to draw its statistics (see the Privacy Policy, section Activity statistics). Server owners and admins decide whether it does: it can be turned off for the whole server, or only the counts per member, with `!statsconfig` or in the dashboard, and every counter can be deleted.
  2. By leaving it on, the owners and admins of a server are responsible for telling their members that their activity is counted and for following the law that applies to them about it. Any member can ask not to be counted with `!stats privacy`, and Petto then stops counting them everywhere.
  3. The statistics are a help, not a record: counts can be missing (the bot was off, the server turned counting off for a while, someone opted out) and are provided as they are. Do not use them to harass, expose, discriminate against or pressure a person, and do not publish a member's counts without that member's agreement.

5. Your own pictures and badges

  1. With a user plan you can upload a picture for your rank card and badges of your own. You are responsible for what you upload: it must be yours or you must have the right to use it, and it must not contain nudity or sexual content, violence, hate, harassment, illegal content or the personal data of other people.
  2. Every picture is checked by an automated service and can be reviewed by the team before anyone else sees it. The team can refuse, hide or delete a picture or badge, and can stop a person from uploading more, when these rules are broken.
  3. Streaks count messages the way each server sets it, by the day of Colombia time (GMT-5); they are a game, not a record, and the server can reset them.

6. Acceptable use

  1. Petto may not be used to harass, spam, or distribute illegal content.
  2. It may not be used to evade a ban or a Discord Trust & Safety action, for example to keep doing through the bot what a ban or a restriction stopped someone from doing.
  3. It may not be used to automate abuse against Discord or any third-party service Petto connects to, such as using its commands or integrations to flood a service with requests or messages.
  4. Access can be revoked from a server or user found doing this.

7. Petto Premium and payments

  1. Petto Premium is an optional paid subscription managed through Polar. Petto stays free to add and to use without it.
  2. The current price, billing interval, included server slots, renewal, cancellation, and any refund terms are shown at checkout before payment, so you can review them before you pay.
  3. Every plan has the same Premium features; a plan only changes how many servers it covers.
  4. You can manage payment details, invoices, receipts, and cancellation from the billing portal. It opens with Manage billing on the Premium page of the dashboard, once you have made your first purchase through Polar.
  5. You can check your Premium status in Discord at any time with `!premium`.

8. Purchases and refunds

  1. Premium is paid through Polar and can be cancelled at any time.
  2. When you cancel, Premium stays active until the end of the period you already paid, and it is not renewed after that.
  3. Payments are not refunded, except for charges made twice or by mistake, or when Premium never activated. If one of those happens to you, open a ticket in the Petto support server with the receipt.
  4. The full rules are in the Purchases and Refunds page (petto.sbs/refunds), which is part of these terms.

9. Third-party services

  1. Petto runs on top of Discord, Discloud PostgreSQL, and Cloudflare, among others (see the Credits section on the home page).
  2. In practice, the bot is hosted on Discloud, its data is stored in a PostgreSQL database on Discloud, Premium payments go through Polar, join verification uses Cloudflare Turnstile and Resend (for the email code), and the `/ask` command currently uses Groq.
  3. Using Petto also means your use is subject to those providers, most directly Discord's own Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.
  4. Petto does not control those services, so if one of them has an outage or changes its rules, Petto can be affected too.

10. Intellectual property

  1. The Petto name, the duck mascot, and this site's content belong to the Petto project.
  2. Using Petto or this site does not transfer any of them to you.
  3. The code Petto is built with is credited, not claimed; third-party tools and libraries keep their own licenses.
  4. That is why the Credits section names the tools and services Petto is built on, and each of them stays under the terms set by its own authors.

11. No warranty

  1. Petto is offered without any warranty of uptime, accuracy, or fitness for a particular purpose.
  2. In practice, the bot can be offline for a while, a command can give a wrong result, and a feature may not fit exactly what your server needs.
  3. Back up anything you cannot afford to lose, and do not depend on Petto as the only copy of anything important to your server.
  4. For example, keep your own copy of important rules, messages, and settings. A Petto Vault backup can be downloaded as a JSON file with `!backup export`, so you can keep it outside Petto.

12. Limitation of liability

  1. To the extent allowed by law, Petto and the people who build it are not liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from using or being unable to use the bot.
  2. This includes lost data, lost roles, or moderation actions taken through it.
  3. For example, if the bot is offline when it should have given a role, or a moderation action set up by staff hits the wrong member, Petto is not liable for what follows from it.
  4. This limit applies only as far as the law allows, so it does not remove a right that the law where you live gives you and that cannot be waived.

13. Termination

  1. A server owner can remove Petto at any time by kicking the bot.
  2. You do it from the member list of the server, like with any other member. What happens to the server data after the bot leaves is explained in the Privacy Policy, section Data retention.
  3. Petto's team can also stop serving a specific server or user for abuse, legal reasons, or repeated violations of these terms, with or without notice.
  4. For example, the team can make the bot leave that server.

14. Governing law

  1. These terms are governed by the laws of Colombia and by general principles of fair use and good faith between the project and the servers running it.
  2. This does not limit any right you have by law where you live.
  3. In practice, this means using Petto for what it is meant for, without abusing it, and reading these terms honestly, by their purpose and not by loopholes.
  4. They are applied consistently regardless of where a server or its members are located.
  5. For personal information, Petto follows the principles of Canadian privacy law (PIPEDA), as the Privacy Policy explains.

15. Dashboard and accounts

  1. The web dashboard uses Discord login, so you sign in with your Discord account and do not create a separate password for Petto.
  2. You may only manage servers where Discord gives you the Manage Server or Administrator permission. Your permissions are checked on every page, so if you lose that permission in Discord, you also lose access to that server in the dashboard.
  3. You are responsible for everything done from your account.
  4. Do not share your session or try to reach servers you do not manage. On a shared device, log out when you are done.
  5. Access can be limited or removed if the dashboard is misused.

16. Premium slots and assignment

  1. A Premium subscription includes a number of server slots that you assign to servers from the dashboard.
  2. You choose them on the Premium page of the dashboard. You can only select servers where you have Manage Server or Administrator and where Petto has been added, and a selection becomes active after Polar confirms the subscription.
  3. When a subscription ends, is canceled, or a slot is removed, the Premium features of that server turn off at the end of the paid period.
  4. Your server data is kept, but Premium-only options stop working until Premium is active again. In the meantime, the server keeps working with the free features of Petto.

17. Backups and restores

  1. Petto Vault backups are snapshots of a server configuration. A backup made with `!backup create` saves roles, channels, permissions, emojis, and server settings.
  2. You are responsible for choosing what to restore, because a restore can overwrite current settings.
  3. A restore with `!backup restore` requires Administrator, and Petto always asks you to confirm it first. The Merge mode restores without deleting anything, while the Replace mode also deletes what the backup does not have.
  4. Petto does not promise that a backup can be restored in a server that changed a lot since it was created. Check your backups with `!backup list` and choose the one that matches what you need.

18. Join verification

  1. A server can ask its members to pass checks before they get in: a captcha and, if the server turns them on, checks of the Tor network, of alt accounts, of the Discord account and a code sent to an email address.
  2. Whether to use them, and what happens to a member who does not pass one, is a decision and a responsibility of the server's staff, not of Petto. Petto does not promise that a check is always right: a member can be stopped or flagged by mistake (for example, because they share a connection with someone else), and the server's staff should be ready to fix it.
  3. When you verify with an email code, use an address that is yours. You may not use another person's address, ask for codes to send them to addresses that are not yours, or try to flood an inbox. Petto limits how many codes it sends and may refuse any address.
  4. The code is sent with Resend, and the data involved is described in the Privacy Policy, in Join verification.

19. Content you submit

  1. You are responsible for the content you submit through Petto, including reports, ticket messages, embeds, custom commands, and form answers.
  2. That includes what you write with commands such as `!report`, `!embed`, or `!customcommand`, and what you write inside a ticket.
  3. Do not submit content that you do not have the right to share, such as images, text, or files that belong to someone else and that you have no permission to use.
  4. Do not include passwords, tokens, or payment details. If you need help with a payment, share the receipt, never your card number.

20. Content you upload to your profile (user content policy)

  1. Petto lets some people upload their own content to their profile: backgrounds, images or GIFs for the rank card, images for the progress bar and their own badges. This policy covers all of it.
  2. Before the first upload you must read this policy and press I agree. If you press I do not agree you can keep using Petto, but you cannot upload content.
  3. What you upload, you upload by your own choice and with your own consent. By uploading you state that you made it or that you have the right to use it, and that it does not break anyone else's rights.
  4. If what you upload infringes someone's copyright or other rights, the responsibility is yours, not Petto's. Petto does not choose, create or endorse what you upload.
  5. When you agree, the email linked to your Discord account is saved as your contact email, so we can reach you if someone makes a claim about something you uploaded. It is used only for that. See Contact and deletion requests in the Privacy Policy.
  6. Petto reviews every image, and every frame of a GIF, before it is shown. The review only looks for content that is not allowed: sexual content, anything sexual involving minors, extreme violence, hate, illegal content and content that exposes someone's private data. It is not used for any other purpose.
  7. Content that involves minors is never kept or shown. It is blocked at once and reported to the authorities as the law requires, and the person loses the ability to upload.
  8. If a rights holder sends a valid claim, Petto removes the content, tells you at your contact email, and can remove the function from accounts that repeat. If you think the claim is wrong you can answer with your reasons.
  9. Petto can remove any content and block the upload function of any account that breaks these terms.
  10. Which law: Petto is run from Colombia and these terms follow Colombian law, in particular Ley 23 de 1982 and Decision 351 of 1993 of the Andean Community on copyright. As a reference for how claims are handled, Petto also follows the notice-and-notice system of Canada's Copyright Act (sections 41.25 and 41.26), the notice-and-action rule of the European Union's Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, article 16) and the notice-and-takedown procedure of section 512 of the United States Copyright Act (DMCA).
  11. To make a claim, write to the contact in the Contact section with the work, where it appears and your details.

21. Applications and forms

  1. Applications for staff, developer, manager, or partner roles are sent to the Petto team for review, through the Apply page (petto.sbs/apply).
  2. Sending an application does not guarantee a role, a reply, or a partnership.
  3. Answers must be truthful, and the team can reject an application for false information or for any reason it considers valid.
  4. How the answers are delivered and kept is explained in the Privacy Policy, section Applications and forms.

22. Partners

  1. The Partners page (petto.sbs/partners) lists projects that work with Petto.
  2. A listing is not an endorsement of a partner: being on the page does not mean that Petto checks, guarantees, or answers for what that partner does.
  3. Its information can be out of date, so check the details on the partner's own site or server before relying on them.
  4. Partners are responsible for their own services, and their own terms apply to them. If you have a problem with a partner's service, contact that partner.

23. Feedback

  1. If you send suggestions or ideas, Petto may use them without owing you payment or credit.
  2. You can send them on the feedback board (petto.sbs/feedback), where you can also vote on the ideas of others.
  3. Suggestions do not transfer ownership of your own work. Sharing an idea does not give Petto your code, art, or anything else you made.

24. Severability

  1. If any part of these terms cannot be enforced, the rest stays in force.
  2. For example, if a law where you live makes one rule invalid, only that rule stops applying, and every other section still applies.
  3. Not enforcing a rule at a given moment does not mean the rule is waived. The team can still apply it later.

25. Embed Builder

  1. Embed Builder (embed-generator.petto.sbs) is a Petto product, and these terms apply to it.
  2. You are responsible for the messages you send with it and for keeping your bot token and webhook URLs safe.
  3. Anyone who has your bot token can control your bot, and anyone who has a webhook URL can post through it, so do not share them or paste them anywhere you do not trust.
  4. Embed Builder keeps them only in your browser's local storage, and clearing your browser data removes them.
  5. Sending a message through it is also subject to Discord's own Terms of Service, and Petto Team is not responsible for messages sent with your credentials.

26. AI answers (beta)

  1. `/ask` is an optional beta feature: any member can type a question with `/ai ask` or `!ask`, and an AI model answers it in the chat. Server staff can turn it off for their server or for some channels, and Petto can limit or stop it at any time.
  2. The answer comes from software, not from a person. It can be wrong or out of date, it has no internet, and it must not be relied on for legal, medical, financial or safety advice. Every answer says that it was written by an AI.
  3. What you type in a question is sent to a third-party AI provider to write the answer, as the Privacy Policy explains. Do not put passwords, tokens, card numbers or other people's private information in a question.
  4. Do not try to make it ignore its rules, or to get abusive, illegal, sexual or misleading content from it. Free members have a daily limit, and the feature can be removed from a person or a server that abuses it.
  5. It has no powers: it only writes text, and nothing it writes is a promise by Petto or by the server.
  6. The feature is in beta: it can change, be limited, or stop at any time, and it is offered without any guarantee of availability or accuracy.

27. Changes

  1. These terms may change as Petto changes, for example when plans or prices change.
  2. Meaningful changes will be reflected in the "last updated" date above, so you can check that date to see whether the terms changed since you last read them.
  3. Continuing to use the bot after an update means you accept the current version. If you do not agree with a new version, you can stop using Petto and remove it from your server.

28. Contact

  1. Legal questions about these terms can be sent to legal@kirzu.sbs.
  2. Everything else can go through the support server, linked from the Community menu and also reachable at petto.sbs/support.
  3. For a question about a payment, open a ticket there and say which payment it is about.
